hints: At the maximum point $M$, differentiate $y=x^2\cos3x$ and set the derivative equal to zero.
The product and chain rules give $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=2x\cos3x-3x^2\sin3x$.
At $x=a>0$, rearrange the stationary-point equation to $\tan3a=\dfrac{2}{3a}$.
Apply $\tan^{-1}$ and isolate $a$, using the stated interval to select the relevant angle.
walkthrough:
Differentiate $y = x^2\cos(3x)$ using the product rule and chain rule:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(x^2)\cos(3x) + x^2\dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(\cos(3x)) = 2x\cos(3x) - 3x^2\sin(3x)$$

Set $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = 0$ at the stationary point $M$ where $x = a$:
$$2a\cos(3a) - 3a^2\sin(3a) = 0$$

Divide by $a > 0$ and rearrange the equation:
$$3a\sin(3a) = 2\cos(3a)$$
$$\dfrac{\sin(3a)}{\cos(3a)} = \dfrac{2}{3a}$$
$$\tan(3a) = \dfrac{2}{3a}$$

Take the inverse tangent and divide by 3 to isolate $a$:
$$3a = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2}{3a}\right)$$
$$a = \dfrac{1}{3}\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2}{3a}\right)$$

hints: Use the fixed-point equation from part (a) directly as an iteration in radians.
Set $a_{n+1}=\dfrac13\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2}{3a_n}\right)$ and choose a reasonable positive starting value in $0<a<\pi/6$.
Record every iterate to 4 decimal places and continue until successive values settle sufficiently to justify rounding $a$ to 2 decimal places.
walkthrough:
State the iterative formula based on part (a):
$$a_{n+1} = \dfrac{1}{3}\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2}{3a_n}\right)$$

Choose starting value $a_1 = 0.5$ and compute iterations to 4 decimal places in radians:
$$a_2 = \dfrac{1}{3}\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2}{3(0.5)}\right) = \dfrac{1}{3}\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{4}{3}\right) \approx \dfrac{1}{3}(0.927295) = 0.3091$$

Round the final answer correct to 2 decimal places:
$$a = 0.36$$
